title: Chemistry — Pure and impure substances
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for KS3 Science (chemistry) (status of the source: authored-reviewed-reverified-2026-10-08). assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Diffusion
items.clue: Particles spread out and mix by their own random movement.

items.label: Chromatography
items.clue: Separating the dyes in an ink as water soaks up a strip of paper.

items.label: Collision
items.clue: When two moving particles bump into each other and change direction

items.label: Filtration
items.clue: Pouring a mixture through paper in a funnel to trap an insoluble solid.

questions.stem: In the particle model, what causes diffusion?

options.text: Particles that want to spread out
A push from wind or stirring
Particles reacting with each other
Particles moving about at random

questions.explanation: Yes. Particles in liquids and gases move about all the time in all directions. This random movement makes them spread out and mix, with nothing pushing them.

questions.stem: You want to get back both the water and the salt from salty water. Which method should you use?

options.text: Separate it by distillation
Separate it by evaporation
Separate it by filtration
Separate it by chromatography

questions.explanation: Yes. Distillation boils off the water and cools the vapour in a condenser to collect it as pure water, while the salt stays behind in the flask.

questions.stem: How does a pure solid melt?

options.text: Over a range of temperatures
At 0 °C, just as ice does
Only at a very hot temperature
At exactly one temperature

questions.explanation: Yes. A pure solid melts at one sharp, fixed temperature, its melting point. The temperature stays the same until it has all melted.

questions.stem: In the particle model, why is diffusion faster at a higher temperature?

options.text: The particles move about faster
The particles all get a bit bigger
The heat pushes the particles along
The particles want to spread out more

questions.explanation: Yes. At a higher temperature the particles move faster, so they spread out and mix more quickly.

questions.stem: Salty water is poured through filter paper in a funnel. What comes through the paper?

options.text: Water, with the salt melted in it
Water, with the salt dissolved in it
Only water, as the paper traps the salt
Only water, as the salt has vanished away

questions.explanation: Yes. The dissolved salt is spread out as particles far smaller than the holes in the paper, so it passes through with the water. Nothing is separated.

questions.stem: Two inks are tested by paper chromatography. Ink S gives one spot. Ink T gives three spots. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: S is a mixture, and T may be pure
Both are pure, since each is one ink
T's dyes were made by the test
S may be pure; T is a mixture

questions.explanation: Yes. A pure substance gives only one spot, so S may be pure (more tests would check). T separates into three spots, so it contains at least three dyes: it is a mixture.

questions.stem: A drop of ink is put into a beaker of still water. A day later, the colour is even all through the water. What are the ink particles doing now?

options.text: They have stopped, as they are spread out
They have joined water in a new compound
They are still moving in all directions
They are still looking for more room

questions.explanation: Yes. In a liquid the particles never stop moving: they move about at random in all directions. The colour stays even because, on average, as many ink particles move one way as the other.

questions.stem: A mixture contains sand, salt and water. Which plan gives dry salt with no sand in it?

options.text: Filter, then evaporate the liquid that comes through
Evaporate first, then filter the dry solid that is left
Filter, then scrape the salt off the filter paper
Distil, then collect the salt that drips out

questions.explanation: Yes. Filtering traps the insoluble sand while the dissolved salt passes through with the water. Evaporating that filtrate then leaves the salt as dry crystals.

questions.stem: Pure water boils at 100 °C. How does salty water boil?

options.text: Lower than 100 °C, over a range
Higher than 100 °C, over a range
At exactly 100 °C, like water
At one fixed temperature above 100 °C

questions.explanation: Yes. Salty water is a mixture, so it boils over a range of temperatures, starting above 100 °C and rising as the water boils away.

questions.stem: Diffusion is much faster in gases than in liquids. Which explains this, using the particle model?

options.text: Gas particles move quickly through large gaps
Gas particles are smaller than liquid ones
Gas particles are carried along by air currents
Gas particles try to spread themselves out evenly

questions.explanation: Gas particles move quickly and are far apart, so they travel further between collisions and mix faster.
